name: Jeroham
overview: Jeroham was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, known primarily as the father of Ibneiah. His mention in Scripture is brief and focused on his role within his family lineage. No additional personal details or notable deeds are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeroham means 'he will be compassionate,' reflecting a meaningful Hebrew proper name. This name was not given directly by God but carries a hopeful and gracious connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Jeroham is identified explicitly as a descendant of Benjamin and is noted as the father of Ibneiah. Scripture does not provide further details about his family beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Jeroham's significance lies in his place within the genealogical record of the tribe of Benjamin. As the father of Ibneiah, his mention helps preserve the lineage important to Israel's history. Though no specific acts or roles are attributed to him, his inclusion in the biblical record underscores the value of faithful genealogical documentation.
